findings.summary: Both ADXL362 interrupt pins double as inputs: keep FILTER_CTL EXT_SAMPLE and EXT_CLK clear, and map activity through INTMAP2
findings.description: INT2 (pin 9) now drives PA0/WKUP1; INT1 (pin 11) is unconnected. INT2 also serves as the synchronized-sampling input (FILTER_CTL bit 3 EXT_SAMPLE); setting that bit turns the wake pin into an ADXL362 input that nothing drives except PA0, which is configured as a wake input. INT1 is the external-clock input (FILTER_CTL EXT_CLK); setting that bit leaves an undriven, floating input on an unconnected pin, a leakage path in a 10 uA design. With both bits at their reset value 0, both pins are push-pull outputs and the open INT1 is harmless. Designer confirmed 2026-10-14 that the part is used for activity detection only, never in measurement mode.
findings.recommendation: Firmware: map ACT (and INACT if used) via INTMAP2 (0x2B), leave EXT_SAMPLE and EXT_CLK at 0, and match the PA0 WKUP1 wake polarity (PWR_CR4.WP1) to INTMAP2.INT_LOW.

datasheet.quote: INT2 also serves as an input for synchronized sampling.
INT1 also serves as an input for external clocking.
1 = the INT2 pin is used for external conversion timing control.

computation.description: Netlist re-exported after the INT1 -> INT2 change
computation.result: U2.9 INT2 -> /WKUP1 -> U302.6 (PA0); U2.11 INT1 unconnected

findings.summary: ADXL362 on USART2 synchronous mode (AF7, PA4/PA2/PA3, CS on PA1) carries over from the ADXL367 unchanged: same SPI mode 0, MSB-first protocol
findings.description: The MCU pins are identical to the parent's (stm32_pinmap.py: pin numbering matches the package, 25 GPIO pins checked against STM32_open_pin_data). ADXL362 SPI is CPHA = CPOL = 0 (p.21) with fCLK 2.4 kHz to 8 MHz (Table 10, p.23; the minimum applies only when using the FIFO), and CS must stay low for the whole transaction, which a GPIO CS on PA1 guarantees while USART2 inserts start/stop gaps between bytes. Command bytes 0x0A write / 0x0B read are the same as the ADXL367's. The ADXL367 caveat 'SCLK low selects I2C' no longer applies: the ADXL362 is SPI-only.
findings.recommendation: Firmware: keep the existing USART2 configuration (MSBFIRST, CPOL=0/CPHA=0, LBCL), keep SCK at or below 8 MHz, and replace the ADXL367 driver: PARTID 0xF2 (vs 0xF7), 12-bit data, different FIFO, filter and power-control registers.

datasheet.quote: The SPI timing scheme follows CPHA = CPOL = 0.

computation.result: pin numbering matches the package (25 GPIO pins checked); PA2/PA3/PA4 = ACCEL_MOSI/MISO/SCK, PA1 = ACCEL_nCS; the only collisions are the known SPI1 LPS/AT25 ones, resolved by SPI3 (AF6) for the flash

findings.summary: ADXL362 Rev. G power-cycling rule: VS and VDD I/O must fall to <= 100 mV for >= 200 ms before power is reapplied
findings.description: Rev. G added VRESET, hold-time and rise-time requirements (p.40). On this tag they apply only at cell insertion or when the connecting board powers VIN through J201. The 91 uF of VIN bulk (C4 + C404 + C6) holds charge after a cell is pulled, so a quick re-insert can violate VRESET and leave the accelerometer in an undefined state.
findings.recommendation: Wait several seconds before re-inserting a cell or re-mating the tag. Firmware should issue a soft reset (0x52 to SOFT_RESET, 0x1F) at boot as a belt-and-braces measure.

datasheet.quote: VDD I/O supply must be discharged to a voltage VRESET ≤ 100 mV

computation.description: Bulk capacitance on VIN from the BOM
computation.result: C4 22 uF + C404 22 uF + C6 47 uF = 91 uF
